# Windows PowerShell 5.1 Scripting

Rules for unattended PowerShell scripts on Windows (Windows PowerShell 5.1,
`powershell.exe`). Each rule: pattern, why, when to apply.

> Learned while building an autonomous agent harness on Windows 11.

## Run Every Subprocess With a Timeout and Kill Guard

**Pattern:** start the process with `Start-Process -PassThru`, touch
`$null = $p.Handle` immediately, call `$p.WaitForExit(<ms>)`, and on timeout
run `taskkill /T /F /PID $p.Id` to kill the whole tree.

```powershell
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $args -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden
$null = $p.Handle                       # cache the handle or ExitCode is $null
if (-not $p.WaitForExit(120000)) {
    & taskkill.exe /T /F /PID $p.Id | Out-Null
    throw "timeout: $exe"
}
$p.ExitCode
```

**Why:** without the cached handle, `ExitCode` reads `$null` after exit.
Without the guard, one hung process stalls the whole run.

**When:** every child process in an unattended script, including elevated and
GUI processes.

## Put Non-Trivial Logic in a Script File

**Pattern:** write the logic to a `.ps1` and run it with
`powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <script>`.
Do not use a long inline `-Command`.

**Why:** complex inline PowerShell triggers permission prompts ("could not
fully check your permission rules") even in bypass mode, and quoting breaks
across shells.

**When:** anything beyond a one-line command.

## Git Calls: `Continue`, Then Check `$LASTEXITCODE`

**Pattern:** set `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'` around native `git`
calls and test `$LASTEXITCODE` explicitly.

**Why:** git writes informational text (for example CRLF warnings) to stderr.
Under `Stop`, PowerShell 5.1 turns that into a terminating error and aborts a
script whose git command succeeded.

**When:** any native command that writes progress or warnings to stderr.

## Small Traps

- **Case-sensitive rules:** use `-cmatch` / `-ceq`. `-match` and `-eq` ignore case.
- **Function names:** never name a function like a built-in alias (`r`, `rm`,
  `sc`, `rd`, `del`). The alias wins silently.
- **BOM-free files:** `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes a BOM in 5.1. Use
  `[IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $text, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false))`.
- **Reading piped JSON:** piped text may start with a BOM. Strip `﻿`
  before `JSON.parse` (or `ConvertFrom-Json`).
- **Here-strings:** the closing `'@` / `"@` must be at column 0.

## Background Console Programs: `conhost.exe --headless`

**Pattern:** launch background or scheduled console programs as
`conhost.exe --headless <program> <args>`.

**Why:** `-WindowStyle Hidden` still flashes a console window that can steal
focus from the user's active window.

**When:** scheduled tasks, watchdogs, and any console process started while a
person may be working at the machine.
